Where this sits

Part of the Authority’s Future Security and Resilience programme.
It started as a power factor study about losses…

Power system security has two dimensions

Frequency: a complete, automatic chain

Voltage: no last resort when it rises

Inertia matters. It is not the binding constraint.

“even with significantly higher inertia values, the loss of system synchronism would not have been avoided…” ENTSO-E expert panel, Iberian blackout final report, 20 March 2026
The Iberian panel records that modelling the transmission–distribution interfaces accurately would need “information on load composition”, without pursuing it.
The constraint tightening fastest is
reactive power and voltage.

29 years of reactive power. It turned in 2016.

Night and evening fell together.
It is there whether or not anything is switched on.

It’s the cables!

0.97R². Twelve years on one straight line.
…isn’t it?

Hang on. It’s not the cables.

  • Cable-free’ish networks drift too
  • Same drift per MW at every cable share
  • Cables: about a fifth of the drift

It scales with connections

Houses and businesses: about half each

Six houses for every business, and about half the deepening each.
Same socket. Same always-plugged job.
Near-symmetric magnitudes. Opposite sign.
Left: iron-core linear. Right: switched-mode.

Where it arrives first

The cable charging was always there. The load used to cover part of it.
Charging goes as voltage squared, not load, so it never goes away. An undergrounding network with a modernising fleet gets there first.

The international evidence

No defence plan carried a measure addressed to voltage rising.

What cascades is the absorption

Two loops, and what changes when the demand leads

Europe and New Zealand: what differs

EuropeNew Zealand
The rulesthe light-load leading condition written into law, 2016no provision addressed to it. The one power factor term applies at regional peak only
The measurementnone published, for either system examined29 years of it
The plantSpain: about 90 reactors, 42% disconnected when it matteredSTATCOMs and reactors added, and circuit switching at light load now needed less
Transpower is managing the symptom well. But the driver is still growing, and the rules have not caught up.

The System Operator has named the two conditions

“if there is a reduction in the minimum loads or an increase in capacitive load power factor … these issues may become unmanageable using current operational measures and reactive plant” N-1 Thermal and Voltage Study, System Security Forecast
Everything so far is a measurement of the second one.

Created here. Counted here. Absorbed here.

A distribution business owns the whole of that path.

The answer is already on the wall

the device, unreachable in both directions
Volt-var is already in the standard. What we will need from it overnight is absorption, not injection.

A whole-of-industry question

Two European blackouts, and the statistics that showed it wasn’t the cables that moved it, to make this a security question.
A potential power system security issue that reaches from the engineers modelling demand at ICPs, through distribution and transmission planning, to system operation.
A capacitor smaller than a coin, and tens of millions of them!
100 MVAr electromagnets at the other end of the wire!
No one party can see the whole path.

Thank you · Ngā mihi

Have you tapped down, or changed standing taps, and what drove it?
